theater: 齊郡豺狗山（山東臨淄境）

battle.name: 左孝友起義
battle.theater: 齊郡豺狗山（山東臨淄境）
battle.brief: 大業十年(614)冬,隋煬帝三征高句麗、群盜並起,齊郡賊帥左孝友聚眾十萬屯豺狗山(通鑑作蹲狗山),郡丞張須陀列營封其山道糧道,孝友窘迫出降,餘黨四人各萬計亦被逐一掃平。卡面科林斯青銅盔屬希臘重裝步兵舊式裝備,東亞無對應物,只作對照:山頭戴的是隋軍鐵兜鍪與叛軍布纏頭。

kit.name: 科林斯青銅盔
kit.history: 全正面開眼的青銅盔。看得見的代價是：戴它的人只能靠隊形活。

countries: 左孝友起義爆發於隋煬帝大業十年(614)冬,地點在齊郡豺狗山(《資治通鑑》作「蹲狗山」),約在今山東淄博臨淄以北的山區。叛方不是國家,也不是有綱領的政權,而是由左孝友出面,以齊郡本地的饑民、逃戶、亡命之徒與豪強私兵拼成的一支臨時聯軍;通鑑貶稱其首領為「賊帥」,記眾十萬,屯山不攻,靠險阻、流動與劫掠糧食維持。首領被逼降後,這支聯軍立即碎成四塊:解象、王良、鄭大彪、李充各領眾萬計,分屯四處,互不隸屬,說明它從無統一編制與指揮系統。官方的結構則是隋朝自中央到郡縣的整套機器:皇帝楊廣正第三次征高句麗,精兵東調,京師宿衛遠在涿郡與遼東;齊郡郡丞張須陀以郡兵列營逼山,靠郡倉現糧、郡兵骨幹與臨時招募的猛士作戰。同一時段的亂局說明官軍如何捉襟見肘:延安賊帥劉迦論眾十萬自稱皇王建元大世;孟讓自長白山率眾十餘萬據都梁宮、阻淮為固,江都丞王世充設五柵拒之;汲郡賊帥王德仁擁眾數萬保林慮山;離石胡劉苗王反,眾至數萬;邯鄲賊帥楊公卿率八千抄襲皇帝車駕後隊;涿郡賊帥盧明月眾十餘萬屯軍祝阿。郡與郡不能相救,一郡之丞能平一山已屬例外,制度層面的崩解遠早於王朝本身。
countriesEn: The rising of Zuo Xiaoyou broke out in the winter of 614 CE, the tenth year of the Daye era of Emperor Yang of Sui, at Zhaigou Mountain in Qi commandery (written 'Dòugǒu shān' in the Zizhi Tongjian), in the hills north of what is now Linzi in Shandong. The insurgents were neither a state nor a movement with a programme: they were a temporary coalition assembled by Zuo Xiaoyou out of famine victims, tax absentees, outlaws and the private retainers of local strongmen. The Tongjian derisively calls their leader a 'bandit chieftain', records a following of one hundred thousand, and shows the rebels sitting on the mountain rather than attacking anything, living on terrain, mobility and plundered grain. Once the leader was forced down, the coalition broke into four pieces: Jie Xiang, Wang Liang, Zheng Dbiao and Li Chong each led a following counted in the thousands, each holding its own ground, none subordinate to the others, which shows there was never a unified establishment or command system. On the government side stood the whole Sui machine, from court down to commandery: Emperor Yang was on his third Goguryeo campaign with the picked troops pulled eastward and the capital guards far away at Zhuojun and in Liao-dong, so the defence of Qi commandery fell to its deputy administrator Zhang Xutuo, who camped below the mountain with commandery soldiers, grain drawn from the commandery granaries and toughs hired on the spot. The parallel disorders of the same months show how stretched the government was: Liu Jialun in Yan'an with a hundred thousand men, proclaiming himself king and founding the Daishi era; Meng Rang coming off Changbai Mountain with more than a hundred thousand and holding Duliang Palace across the Huai, against whom the administrator of Jiangdu, Wang Shichong, set up five stockades; Wang Deren of Jijun with several thousands entrenched at Linlu Mountain; Liu Miaowang raising tens of thousands in Lishi; Yang Gongqing of Handan with eight thousand raiding the imperial convoy from behind; and Lu Mingyue of Zhuojun with more than a hundred thousand at Zhua. Commandery would not support commandery, and a single deputy administrator putting down one hill was already exceptional: the institutional collapse came long before the fall of the dynasty itself.
people: 左孝友,齊郡人,隋末起義領袖。通鑑對他只有兩筆:「齊郡賊帥左孝友眾十萬屯蹲狗山」,以及在郡丞張須陀逼迫下「窘迫出降」。他如何聚眾、眾卒名籍、投降後結局,史皆未載,唯可確定的是他兵眾之眾與所據地勢之險。真正主導戰局的是張須陀,《通鑑》作「張須陀」,他書與後世引文又常作「張須臾」。他以郡丞之身統軍出戰,平山之後「威振東夏」,遷齊郡通守,兼領河南道十二郡黜陟討捕大使(他本作「催捕大使」),自此獲得跨郡調兵的名分。同年冬,他又以一萬人邀戰涿郡賊帥盧明月(眾十餘萬,屯祝阿,地在齊郡歷城一帶),相持十餘日而糧盡,諸將無敢應,唯羅士信與歷城秦叔寶請行,二人分將千兵伏於葭叢,待敵全眾追來,躍入其柵,斬關納兵,縱火焚其三十餘柵,大破之,盧明月以數百騎遁走。羅士信是少年驍將,常為前驅;秦叔寶名瓊、以字行,相傳二人每戰士信驅前、叔寶殿後。二人自齊郡的戰陣中嶄露,後轉投瓦崗李密,再入唐軍:叔寶終列凌煙閣,士信則歿於武德四年的洛陽之役。背景人物是皇帝楊廣本人:是年三月出師高句麗時「士卒在道,亡者相繼」,七月次懷遠鎮、八月班師,十一月在金光門外殺朝臣斛斯政、烹其肉使百官分食,又欲如東都,太史令庚質以「比歲伐遼,民實勞弊」進諫。
peopleEn: Zuo Xiaoyou was a native of Qi commandery and a rebel leader at the end of the Sui. The Tongjian devotes him only two lines: 'the bandit chieftain of Qi commandery, Zuo Xiaoyou, with a hundred thousand men stationed at Zhaigou Mountain', and his being 'cornered and forced to surrender' under the pressure of the deputy administrator Zhang Xutuo. How he gathered his men, the roster of his soldiers and what became of him after his surrender are all unrecorded; what can be certain is the size of his following and how strong the position he held. The man who actually decided the battle was Zhang Xutuo, written 'Zhang Xutuo' in the Tongjian and often 'Zhang Xuyu' in other texts and later quotation. He led the army in the field while holding the office of deputy administrator, and after the mountain was taken 'his prestige spread over the eastern lands'; he was promoted to Tongshou of Qi commandery and made incumbent of the twelve commanderies of the Henan circuit as inspector and constable (other copies read 'inquisitor and constable'), which gave him the standing to move troops across commandery borders. In the same winter he met the Zhuojun bandit chief Lu Mingyue, who had more than a hundred thousand men at Zhua in the Licheng area, with a force of ten thousand. They held each other for more than ten days until his own grain ran out; no officer dared answer his question, and only Luo Shixin and Qin Shubao of Licheng volunteered. They took a thousand men and hid them in the reeds, let the enemy pursue in full, climbed over the stockade, cut the gate open to admit the outsiders, and set fire to more than thirty of the enemy enclosures, winning a great victory; Lu Mingyue escaped with a few hundred horsemen. Luo Shixin was a fierce young officer who habitually led the charge; Qin Shubao, whose given name was Qiong and who was known by his courtesy name, is said to have fought in the rearguard while Shixin led. Both made their mark in the fighting at Qi commandery, later joined the ranks of Li Mi at Wagang, and then entered Tang service: Shubao ended among the twenty-four meritorious officials of the Lingyan Pavilion, while Shixin was killed in the fighting at Luoyang in the fourth year of Wude. The figure behind the whole scene is Emperor Yang himself: in the third month of that year, when the army set out for Goguryeo, 'soldiers died on the road one after another'; the court reached Huaiyuan in the seventh month and returned in the eighth; in the eleventh month the emperor killed the minister Huxi Zheng before the Golden Light Gate, boiled his flesh and had the assembled officials eat it, and then wished to travel again to the eastern capital, where the Grand Astrologer Geng Zhi remonstrated that 'for years past the war against Liaodong has exhausted the people; your Majesty should settle and guard the passes within the passes and let the people devote themselves to farming and mulberry for three or five years, and only then will the realm be somewhat abundant'.
kits: 這場戰役裡真正戴在頭上的,不是卡面那頂科林斯青銅盔。該盔鑄於公元前七世紀的希臘,整體銅鑄,鼻脊縱貫,兩側護頰,只留眼孔與呼吸的縫;它是地中海世界最著名的封閉式頭盔,設計前提是重裝步兵靠嚴整隊形、旗幟、口令與傳令手,補回被遮蔽的視野。東亞同源的做法並不晚:春秋戰國的楚墓已出土銅冑,但到隋代,頭盔主材已換成鐵,銅只餘飾面。隋軍裝備以鐵質兜鍪、冑為主,下垂頓項護頸,加護鼻與護頰,內襯皮革綿帛,再配札甲或魚鱗甲片;鎏金銅飾甲片在隋唐墓葬中屢見,敦煌莫高窟第285窟西壁那幅開皇年間的儀仗與騎士圖,是今日所能見到最接近隋軍裝束的同時代圖像之一。叛軍的裝備則明顯不成體系:十萬之眾出自饑民、逃戶與本地私兵,頭上多是布纏頭、皮兜乃至斗笠,甲胄極少,兵器以環首刀、直刀、短槊、矛、弓箭為主,大量農具改造成鋤、斧、叉,攻城器械全無,只在山道與村落間流竄。官軍則有郡兵、縣鄉團練與臨時募來的猛士,長柄槊、弓弩(含蹶張臂弩)、橫刀齊備,營中設木柵、帳幕與糧車,糧秣由郡倉直接供應;通鑑記張須陀與盧明月相持十餘日而「糧盡」幾退,反襯出叛軍靠搶糧、官軍靠現糧的分野。火攻是那年官軍常用的手段,焚柵三十餘座靠的是乾燥木材而非火藥;史冊沒有任何攻城器械投入豺狗山之戰的記載。可以確定的只有一點:科林斯盔在這場戰爭裡不曾出現,它只是把一條「用封閉的面甲換取防護、靠隊形而非眼睛求生」的裝備譜系,擺在隋軍鐵冑與叛軍布纏頭之間作對照。
kitsEn: The helmet actually worn in this campaign was not the Corinthian bronze helmet on the card. That helmet was cast in seventh-century Greece, a single piece of bronze with a central nasal ridge, cheek-pieces closing the sides of the face, and openings only for the eyes and for breathing; it is the most famous closed helmet of the Mediterranean world, and its premise is that heavily armoured infantry recover the vision their closed face denies them through tight formation, standards, shouted orders and hand signals. The East Asian version of the same idea is no later: bronze helmets have been unearthed from Chu tombs of the Spring and Autumn and Warring States periods, but by the Sui the main material of the helmet was iron, with bronze surviving only as decoration. Sui troops wore iron dou and zhou with a falling neck guard, a nasal bar and cheek-pieces, lined with leather and hemp cloth, over lamellar or scale armour; gilt-bronze armour fittings turn up repeatedly in Sui and Tang tombs, and the procession and mounted figures on the west wall of Cave 285 at Dunhuang are among the closest contemporary images of Sui military dress that survive. The rebels had nothing of the kind: of a hundred thousand men drawn from famine victims, absentees and local private retainers, most had cloth wrapped round the head, a leather cap or a straw hat, and almost no armour at all; their arms were ring-pommel sabres, straight blades, short spears, polearms, bows and arrows, with a great many farm tools turned into mattocks, axes and forks. They had no siege equipment at all and simply moved along mountain paths and through villages. The government side had commandery soldiers, county levies and toughs hired on the spot, with long spears, crossbows including the strong-armed draw-bow, and sabres, wooden stockades, tents and supply wagons in the camp, and grain delivered straight from the commandery granaries. The Tongjian records that Zhang Xutuo stood against Lu Mingyue for more than ten days until his own grain was exhausted, which sets the two systems side by side: the rebels lived on what they could take, the government on what it could draw from store. Fire was a standard weapon for the government that year, and the thirty-odd enclosures burnt at Zhua were consumed by dry timber and not by gunpowder. No siege engine is recorded as ever having been used against Zhaigou Mountain. What can be certain is this: the Corinthian helmet never appeared in this war. It simply places a specimen of the closed-visor principle, 'trading a sealed face for protection, living by formation rather than by eyesight', between the Sui iron helmet and the rebels' cloth headgear.
tactics: 起義一方的戰術,史籍留下的筆墨極少,能確定的只有「屯」與「降」兩個動作:左孝友眾十萬不據城、不攻城,退守豺狗山這處山勢,以險阻與距離拖住官軍,待糧道斷絕、援兵不至再作打算;四支黨羽在他投降後仍各自為戰、各自盤踞,說明這支聯軍從無統一編制與指揮系統,是一種鬆散的武裝聚合,一旦首領被逼降,便迅速崩解。官軍這邊的做法可以從同卷記載的祝阿之戰看出完整邏輯:張須陀不急於強攻,而是列營逼近、封斷山道與糧道,把「餓」當作主要武器;對上十餘萬眾的盧明月,他先以一萬人與之相持,故意示弱以保存實力;糧道將盡時他不與部下議死戰,而是自問「此誠危事,誰能往者」,把最危險的奇襲交給兩個年輕人:羅士信、秦叔寶率千兵預伏葭叢,待敵全軍追擊才躍入柵門,斬關納兵,縱火焚燒三十餘柵,然後主力回軍反擊,把追兵打散。整個過程是典型的中國式野戰邏輯:先以少量兵力與營柵牽制,再以火攻與突襲改變戰局,最後由主力收割,全線不作正面硬撼;糧草是被當作變量計算的,地形與伏擊是取勝的關鍵,將士的膽量與體力則決定那一步能不能走完。對比之下,官軍戴封閉兜鍪在視線受阻的夜襲與亂軍中同樣脆弱,這正是科林斯盔那一代設計者面對的難題;只是隋軍所倚靠的不是面甲,而是柵牆、火光與旗號,以及把命令用嗓子和旗子送出去的能力。
tacticsEn: The tactics of the insurgents leave very few strokes in the historical record, and only two actions can be established: to 'garrison' and to 'surrender'. Zuo Xiaoyou's hundred thousand men neither took a city nor attacked one; they withdrew to Zhaigou Mountain and used the terrain and the distance to hold the government army off, waiting for the supply road to be cut and for no reinforcement to come. The four bands that had followed him continued to fight and to hold their own ground even after he had given himself up, which shows that this was a loose aggregation of armed men with no unified establishment and no command system, and that it dissolved quickly once its leader was forced down. The government side is easier to read from the battle at Zhua recorded in the same volume. Zhang Xutuo was in no hurry to storm the position: he camped close, sealed the mountain paths and the supply route, and made hunger his main weapon. Facing Lu Mingyue's hundred thousand and more, he first held a line with ten thousand men, deliberately showing weakness in order to preserve his strength. When the grain was nearly gone he did not call for a desperate fight; he asked instead, 'this is a dangerous business, who will go?', handing the most perilous stroke to two young men. Luo Shixin and Qin Shubao took a thousand men and lay in wait among the reeds; only when the enemy came on in full did they climb over the stockade, cut the gate open to let their own men in, and set fire to more than thirty enclosures, after which the main body turned and struck the pursuers, scattering them. The whole pattern is typical of Chinese field warfare: a small force and a line of stockades hold the enemy first, fire and a sudden assault then change the situation, and the main body gathers the harvest at the end, with no frontal collision anywhere along the line. Grain is treated as a variable to be calculated, terrain and ambush are the keys to victory, and the nerve and physical stamina of the soldiers decide whether the final step can be taken. By contrast, government troops in closed iron helmets were equally vulnerable at night and in the confusion of a routed army, which is precisely the problem the designers of the Corinthian helmet faced; the Sui answered it not with the face-guard but with stockades, firelight and standards, and with the ability to carry orders by voice and by flag.
data: 可核對的數字集中在《資治通鑑》卷一百八十二。叛方:「齊郡賊帥左孝友眾十萬屯蹲狗山」,兵眾十萬;餘眾分四支,解象、王良、鄭大彪、李充「各萬計」,合計仍以萬計。官方:張須陀所部郡兵一萬人(對盧明月「眾十餘萬」,比例約一比十),奇襲時「使二人分將千兵」,焚敵「三十餘柵」,相持「十餘日」而糧盡;事後授齊郡通守,兼領河南道十二郡黜陟討捕大使,管轄橫跨十二郡。同年大業十年,涿郡賊帥盧明月眾十餘萬、屯軍祝阿(地在齊郡歷城一帶),是通鑑同卷所記;再往前的月份裡,四月董純與彭城賊帥張大虎戰於昌慮,五月延安劉迦論眾十萬建元大世,七月「車駕次懷遠鎮」,八月班師,十一月「殺斛斯政於金光門外」。戶口方面,《隋書·食貨志》載大業年間全國戶增至八百九十萬上下、口約四千六百萬,糧秣堆積如山,卻同時以百餘萬之眾三征高句麗,把丁口與糧秣一併耗在遼東,遂有「役繁而民鮮」之弊。徵召與失散的數字,史書只給出「亡者相繼」與「多失期不至」這類概括,沒有可核的細目,任何精確的傷亡數字都無從推算;山頭那十萬眾究竟耗了多少糧、多久才斷炊,史無一字。
dataEn: The verifiable figures are concentrated in volume 182 of the Zizhi Tongjian. On the insurgent side: 'the bandit chieftain of Qi commandery, Zuo Xiaoyou, with a hundred thousand men stationed at Zhaigou Mountain'; the survivors split into four bands, Jie Xiang, Wang Liang, Zheng Dbiao and Li Chong, each 'counted in the thousands', together still in the tens of thousands. On the government side: Zhang Xutuo's commandery force of ten thousand men, against Lu Mingyue's 'hundred thousand and more', a ratio of roughly one to ten; for the stroke, 'the two of them were given a thousand men each'; 'more than thirty enclosures' were burned; they held each other 'for more than ten days' until the grain ran out. In reward he was made Tongshou of Qi commandery and incumbent over twelve commanderies of the Henan circuit as inspector and constable, a jurisdiction stretching across twelve commanderies. The same volume of the same year records Lu Mingyue, bandit chief of Zhuojun, with more than a hundred thousand men at Zhua in the Licheng area of Qi commandery; earlier in the year, in the fourth month Dong Chun fought the Pengcheng bandit chief Zhang Dahu at Changlu, in the fifth month Liu Jialun of Yan'an raised a hundred thousand men and founded the Daishi era, in the seventh month the imperial carriage reached Huaiyuan, in the eighth the army returned, and in the eleventh month Huxi Zheng was killed before the Golden Light Gate. On population, the Shitui zhi of the Book of Sui records that by the Daye years the households of the empire had risen to about 8.9 million and the population to about 46 million, with grain and silk piled up in the treasuries, all the while three campaigns against Goguryeo mustered more than a million men apiece and spent the labour and the grain of the country in Liao-dong, producing the old complaint that the service was heavy while the people were thinned. For recruitment and desertion the records give only such summaries as 'soldiers died on the road one after another' and 'the greater part of those summoned did not arrive on time'; there are no itemised returns, and no exact casualty figure can be computed. How much grain the hundred thousand on the mountain ate, and how many days it took to starve them, the history does not say.
cause: 這場起義的成因,不能脫開大業十年前後的整體崩解。第一是兵役:隋朝自大業八年起三次征高句麗,史稱首次出征即集兵百餘萬,糧秣自山東、河北直抵涿郡,沿途死亡與逃亡在通鑑中屢見「亡者相繼」的記載;第三次出征正當大業十年,山東精兵被抽調一空,正是左孝友敢於聚眾的時機。第二是徭役與巡幸:煬帝三下江都,造龍舟、徵天下百工,又建東都,人力物力耗竭;同年八月班師後他仍欲如東都,太史令庚質以「比歲伐遼,民實勞弊」進諫,說明朝中已有人看見危機。第三是生計:山東、江南連年水旱失收,饑民扶老攜幼流入道路,左孝友這類本地首領與民間渠帥乘機收編流民,以「屯山不攻」的方式積蓄實力。第四是制度:隋朝郡縣雖有官兵,卻因府兵久已歸農、邊軍遠駐而空虛,地方上真正能打的只有郡丞臨時糾集的兵與募來的猛士,一旦某郡出事,中央無法及時調兵,鄰郡亦各守其土。第五是權力結構:通鑑直書「天下已亂」,煬帝的處置不是討叛而是誅諫臣,十一月殺斛斯政、烹其肉令百官分食,令地方與朝中俱已寒心,起義遂無須更多理由。
causeEn: The causes of this rising cannot be separated from the general breakdown of the years around 614. First, military service: from 608 the Sui fought three campaigns against Goguryeo, the first of them mustering, as the histories put it, more than a million men, with grain and supplies dragged from Shandong and Hebei to Zhuojun, and the Tongjian repeatedly notes men dying on the road; the third campaign fell in 614, and with the picked troops of Shandong drawn away, that was the moment when a man such as Zuo Xiaoyou dared to gather a following. Second, corvée and travel: Emperor Yang made three journeys to Jiangdu, had dragon-boats built and the craftsmen of the empire conscripted, and constructed the eastern capital, draining away labour and materials; even after the army returned in the eighth month he still wished to travel to the eastern capital, and the Grand Astrologer Geng Zhi warned that 'for years past the war against Liaodong has exhausted the people; your Majesty should settle and guard the region within the passes and let the people devote themselves to farming and mulberry for three or five years, and only then will the realm be somewhat abundant', which shows that the court had already seen the crisis. Third, livelihood: repeated floods and droughts had ruined the harvests of Shandong and the lower Yangtze, famine families streamed along the roads, and local strongmen and village leaders such as Zuo Xiaoyou gathered them in, building strength by sitting on a mountain rather than attacking. Fourth, institutions: although commanderies and counties still had official troops, the army was hollow, because the fubing had long since been sent back to the fields and the frontier garrisons stood far away; the only real fighting force in the localities was what a deputy administrator could scrape together locally plus the toughs he hired, and when a commandery rose, the court could not send troops in time while neighbouring commanderies each sat tight on their own ground. Fifth, the structure of power: the Tongjian states plainly that 'the realm was already in disorder', and the emperor's response was not to campaign against the rebels but to execute the men who remonstrated, killing Huxi Zheng in the eleventh month and boiling his flesh for the assembled officials to eat; both the localities and the court were by then cold, and the rising needed no further justification.
impact: 豺狗山之役本身規模不大,卻有三層長遠影響。第一是讓隋朝的郡縣軍事體系又撐了數年:張須陀以郡丞之身平山,事後升授通守並取得河南道十二郡黜陟討捕大使的名號,說明朝廷在崩解過程中不得不把跨郡調兵的權柄下放給地方武人;秦叔寶、羅士信正是在這種地方隊伍中嶄露頭角,後轉投瓦崗李密,再歸唐室,終成唐朝開國將領的骨幹——一場被平息的郡級叛亂,直接把兩名唐室柱石送上了戰場。第二是把隋末亂局從流寇推向割據:左孝友降後,同年通鑑仍記著劉迦論、孟讓、王德仁、劉苗王、楊公卿、盧明月、彭孝才等十餘名叛帥,山東、淮南、河北同時燃燒,瓦崗李密在這批亂軍中崛起,竇建德在河北坐大,三年之後隋室傾覆,新造的唐朝承接了這批因隋末軍制崩壞而散落的兵員與裝備。第三是裝備與制度層面的傳承:隋代以鐵冑、札甲、募兵與郡兵團練為主的配置,經唐初重新整編,部分匯入府兵與州縣兵源,成為唐軍裝備與徵發制度的底子;而「用封閉面甲換取防護、靠隊形與旗號補回視野」的設計邏輯,從科林斯青銅盔一路傳到隋軍兜鍪,再進到唐代明光鎧,始終是東方重裝步兵的基本原理。至於平民,這場戰爭的傷亡與流離並無可靠統計,史書留下的只有「眾十萬」「各萬計」這類兵眾數目,任何更精確的說法都屬臆測。
impactEn: The fighting at Zhaigou Mountain was small in scale, yet it had three long-range effects. First, it kept the commandery-based military system of the Sui alive for a few more years. Zhang Xutuo, who had put down the mountain while holding the office of deputy administrator, was promoted to Tongshou and given the title of inspector and constable over twelve commanderies of the Henan circuit, which shows that, as the regime came apart, the court had no choice but to push the power of moving troops across commandery boundaries down to local military men. Qin Shubao and Luo Shixin made their names in exactly this kind of local force, then moved to the rebel camp of Li Mi at Wagang and afterwards into Tang service, ending up as the backbone of the new dynasty's generals: a single suppressed commandery rising had thrown two pillars of the Tang state straight onto the battlefield. Second, it pushed the late Sui disorder from roving banditry towards territorial separatism. After Zuo Xiaoyou came down, the Tongjian of the same year still names more than a dozen rebel chiefs - Liu Jialun, Meng Rang, Wang Deren, Liu Miaowang, Yang Gongqing, Lu Mingyue, Peng Xiaocai - while Shandong, the Huai valley and Hebei burned at once; Li Mi rose out of these bands at Wagang and Dou Jiande grew strong in Hebei, and three years later the Sui fell and the new Tang state absorbed the soldiers and equipment scattered by the collapse of the Sui military system. Third, it carried on the equipment and institutional inheritance. The Sui configuration of iron helmets, lamellar armour, recruited troops and commandery levies was partly re-tasked in the early Tang and fed into the fubing and the county militia, becoming the base of Tang armaments and of the recruitment system; and the design logic of 'trading a sealed face-guard for protection, recovering the lost sight through formation and signals' runs unbroken from the Corinthian bronze helmet through the Sui iron helmet to the Tang Mingguang armour, and remains the working principle of the heavy infantry of the East. As for the civilians, no reliable count of the dead or of the displaced from this war survives; the histories leave only the troop numbers, 'a hundred thousand' and 'counted in the thousands', and any more precise figure would be invention.
result: 戰果是叛方全敗而官方完勝,代價極小。通鑑的記載很短:郡丞張須陀「列營逼之」,左孝友「窘迫出降」,山頭的十萬眾在斷糧與封山之下瓦解;餘黨解象、王良、鄭大彪、李充各自被張須陀分別掃平,四支合計仍以萬計,至此齊郡地面的主要武裝被清除。官軍方面,張須陀一戰成名,「威振東夏」,由郡丞遷齊郡通守,兼領河南道十二郡黜陟討捕大使,權責與名位同時上揚;同年冬他再以萬人破盧明月十餘萬於祝阿,焚柵三十餘座,兩戰連捷,成為隋末平叛名將中最擅長用奇襲與火攻者之一。齊郡的秩序短期內恢復,郡倉重新供糧,郡兵重新上崗,叛軍所據的豺狗山據點被拔除。但這場勝負只說明局部:大業十年通鑑所載的叛帥至少有十餘名,被平掉的左孝友一支佔不上大數;其餘如孟讓(眾十餘萬)、盧明月(眾十餘萬)、劉迦論(眾十萬)等部,仍在淮南、河北、關中繼續活動,大業十一年之後形勢更壞,至武德元年隋亡、李密與竇建德各自建號,地方割據已成定型。史書未載左孝友降後的結局,只有「窘迫出降」四字;可以確定的是,他交出的並不是性命(史無斬首記載),而是一支尚未成形、隨時會重新聚起的地方武力。
resultEn: The result was a complete defeat for the insurgents and a clean victory for the government, at a very small cost. The Tongjian tells it in two lines: the deputy administrator Zhang Xutuo 'camped and pressed in on him', and Zuo Xiaoyou, 'cornered, came out and surrendered'; the hundred thousand on the mountain came apart under hunger and a closed road; the surviving bands of Jie Xiang, Wang Liang, Zheng Dbiao and Li Chong were each swept up separately by Zhang Xutuo, and together they still numbered in the tens of thousands, so that the main body of armed men on the ground of Qi commandery was cleared away. On the government side Zhang Xutuo made his name in a single action: 'his prestige spread over the eastern lands', and he moved from deputy administrator to Tongshou of Qi commandery and to inspector and constable over twelve commanderies of the Henan circuit, gaining office and standing together. In the same winter he broke Lu Mingyue's hundred thousand and more at Zhua with ten thousand men and burned more than thirty enclosures; two victories in succession made him one of the most skilful of the Sui's pacifying generals in the use of surprise and fire. Order in Qi commandery was restored in the short term, the granaries began to issue grain again, the levies returned to their posts, and the rebel position on Zhaigou Mountain was destroyed. Yet the outcome speaks only of one corner of the picture: the Tongjian of 614 names at least a dozen rebel chiefs, and the band of Zuo Xiaoyou that was put down is not a large share of them. The rest - Meng Rang with more than a hundred thousand, Lu Mingyue with more than a hundred thousand, Liu Jialun with a hundred thousand - went on operating in the Huai valley, in Hebei and in the passes, the situation worsening after 615, until in the first year of Wude the Sui fell and Li Mi and Dou Jiande each assumed a title of their own, and local separatism had taken its final form. The histories do not record what became of Zuo Xiaoyou after his surrender; there is only the four characters 'cornered, came out and surrendered'. What can be certain is that what he handed over was not his life - no beheading is recorded - but a local force that had not yet hardened and could gather itself again at any time.
